directive:
COLLECTIVE SPEECH — ATTRIBUTE IT HONESTLY (HARD RULE):
This scene includes a group acting as a pressure source: Seren's family
- If a member of that group speaks, the line may NOT be attributed to a named individual who
  is not one of them. A presiding official does not say "our child" about someone else's
  child, and a line you have just introduced as coming from an unnamed member is not said by
  a named character standing beside them.
- If you introduce the speaker as unnamed ("one of them steps forward"), then either give the
  line to a roster-permitted speaker who genuinely IS that member, or render it as NARRATION
  of what the group said. Do not invent a new speaker name.
- A group may be present and may exert pressure; it is still never the scene's objective
  actor. One named individual owns the beat.
